basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 2.' and it opens '(Cap. XXII.—Vers. 2.) Et dixit ei Deus: Tolle filium tuum unigenitum, quem diligis,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XXII.—Vers. 2.) Et dixit ei Deus: Tolle filium tuum unigenitum, quem diligis, Isaac, et vade in terram excelsam, et offer illum ibi in holocaustum super unum de montibus quem ego dicam tibi. Difficile est idioma linguae Hebraeae in Latinum sermonem vertere. Ubi nunc dicitur, vade in terram excelsam, in Hebraeo habet, MORIA (מריה), quod Aquila transtulit τὴν καταφανῆ, hoc est, lucidam: Symmachus, τῆς ὀπτασίας, hoc est, visionis. Aiunt ergo Hebraei hunc montem esse in quo postea templum conditum est in area Ornae Jebusaei, sicut et in Paralipomenis scriptum est: Et coeperunt aedificare templum in mense secundo, in secunda die mensis, in monte Moria (II Paralip. III, 1). Qui idcirco illuminans interpretatur et lucens, quia ibi est DABIR (דביר), hoc est, oraculum Dei: et Lex et Spiritus sanctus, qui docet homines veritatem, et inspirat prophetias.
